info.title: LoonFS HTTP API
info.description: Static OpenAPI document for the LoonFS v0 HTTP API.

get.description: Returns `ok` when the server is running and can accept requests.
Returns this process's metrics in Prometheus text exposition format 0.0.4. Unlike `/health` and `/readiness`, the route requires the deployment's bearer token.

Returns `ready` while the server admits new work. Once shutdown begins and publisher admission closes, answers 503 `shutting_down` so load balancers can drain the instance. `/health` stays the liveness probe: it only reports that the process is up.

Lists one page of active checkpoints in checkpoint-id order. Expired checkpoints remain visible until collection releases them. Released checkpoints are omitted. The cursor resumes a live listing and does not create a snapshot.

400.description: Invalid namespace id, limit, or cursor

post.description: Creates a named, user-owned checkpoint record pinning the current namespace view. Every call mints a new record under a new id; the name is a label, not a key. The record is a garbage-collection root until it is released, so routine maintenance should flush the WAL instead. This is a maintenance/admin operation, not a file mutation.

400.description: Invalid namespace id, name, or lifetime

post.description: Releases a user-owned checkpoint pin by id. Idempotent: releasing an already-released or reaped record succeeds. The record is reaped by a later garbage-collection pass; its pinned data becomes collectable only on the pass after that.

200.description: Checkpoint release accepted (including an already released or reaped checkpoint)

400.description: Invalid id, or the checkpoint is owned by another operation

get.description: Returns namespace state together with the current manifest and visible WAL tail.

Returns whether the namespace's grep index is `disabled`, `backfilling`, or `active`, including build progress when available. A namespace that has never enabled the index is `disabled`. This operation requires a deployment that maintains grep indexes and does not change the index.

200.description: Grep index status and build progress

500.description: The grep index is corrupt or its backing store is unavailable

501.description: This deployment does not maintain the grep index

post.description: Disables the namespace's grep root and clears its segment references with one durable compare-and-swap; index maintenance stops on its own once a step reads the disabled root. Explicit grep garbage collection later reclaims the segments. Idempotent. Requires this deployment to maintain the grep index.

200.description: Grep root disabled or already disabled

409.description: Lost a grep root-pointer publication race; retry

500.description: The grep index is corrupt or its backing store is unavailable

501.description: This deployment does not maintain the grep index

post.description: Enables the namespace's grep root and asks this deployment's maintenance runner for the backfill's first step. The response reports the lifecycle and bookkeeping read after the transition: a fresh enable is `backfilling` with the sequence its checkpoint captured, while an already-enabled namespace answers with its current status. Idempotent. Requires this deployment to maintain the grep index.

200.description: Grep root enabled or already enabled

409.description: Lost a grep root-pointer publication race; retry

500.description: The grep index is corrupt or its backing store is unavailable

501.description: This deployment does not maintain the grep index

post.description: Runs one explicit garbage-collection pass over only this namespace's grep-owned extension keyspace. A tombstoned or absent namespace has aged extension state reaped; no grep garbage collection runs implicitly. `max_objects` bounds the reads the pass spends and returns a `next_cursor` when keys remain; resuming re-reads liveness and the grep root, so a cursor only skips enumeration. Requires this deployment to maintain the grep index.

500.description: The grep index is corrupt or its backing store is unavailable

501.description: This deployment does not maintain the grep index

post.description: Runs one bounded maintenance step. Include `metadata_maintenance`, `retention`, or `gc` to select actions. Each selector is an options object, and an empty object uses server defaults. Actions run in that order, and only selected actions appear in the response. At least one action is required. A deleted namespace accepts only `gc`. GC processes up to 1024 candidates by default and returns a cursor when more work remains. A lost root update race is reported as an outcome.

Proves the configured object store honours the create-if-absent, compare-and-swap, visibility, listing, and ranged-read semantics LoonFS depends on, and reports what it found check by check. Nothing runs this implicitly: a probe writes and deletes objects, all of them under a scratch prefix that is not a durable object family, and its last check deletes them and proves the prefix empty. A store that fails a check answers 200 with that check reported `failed` — the probe ran, and the answer is that the store is wrong. Optional capabilities a store declares it lacks answer `unsupported`, which is an answer rather than a fault. This route does not decide whether the deployment may serve presigned direct uploads: that trust comes from the endpoint allowlist, because a probe exercises the server's own request path and never a presigned capability handed to a client.

200.description: Probe completed; per-check outcomes are in the body

get.description: Returns a summary of supported features and limits.

409.description: Namespace already exists or is partial

410.description: Namespace id was deleted and retired

get.description: Returns the current head and retention state for a namespace.

parameters.name: expected_head_seq
parameters.description: Delete only if the namespace head is still at this sequence

get.description: Returns committed changes after a sequence. A snapshot limits the feed to its captured sequence.

parameters.name: after_seq
parameters.description: Return committed changes after this sequence

parameters.name: snapshot_id
parameters.description: End the feed at this snapshot's captured sequence

400.description: Invalid change cursor, limit, snapshot id, non-snapshot checkpoint, or after_seq above the snapshot sequence

409.description: The cursor is older than the retained change history and requires a fresh snapshot

410.description: Namespace deleted or snapshot released or expired

post.description: Applies one commit: an ordered, non-empty list of path operations that commit together as one logical commit, under one commit id that makes retries idempotent. A single-operation call is the one-element case. The first operation that fails aborts the whole request, and a request carrying more than one operation names that operation's position in `details.operation_index`.

get.description: Returns the current file bytes, a retained revision, or the revision captured by a live snapshot.

parameters.name: revision_no
parameters.description: Optional prior revision number; cannot be combined with snapshot_id

parameters.name: snapshot_id
parameters.description: Use the file revision captured by this snapshot

400.description: Invalid path, revision, snapshot id, non-snapshot checkpoint, or revision_no combined with snapshot_id

404.description: Namespace, path, revision, or snapshot not found

410.description: Namespace deleted or snapshot released or expired

post.description: Authorizes one direct read of a file's content object and returns a short-lived presigned GET capability, the resolved revision, and the content reference the client checks the arriving bytes against. `Range` is outside the signature, so one grant serves ranged, resumed, and parallel reads. Deployments that cannot presign answer 501 `not_supported`; the proxied `GET /filesystem/content` route stays available and is capped by `download.max_content_bytes`.

parameters.name: snapshot_id
parameters.description: Use the file revision captured by this snapshot

400.description: Invalid path, revision, snapshot id, non-snapshot checkpoint, or revision_no combined with snapshot_id

404.description: Namespace, path, revision, or snapshot not found

410.description: Namespace deleted or snapshot released or expired

get.description: Lists a directory from the current state or a live snapshot.

parameters.name: include_attributes
parameters.description: Project each entry's attribute map and revision (`true` or `false`). Defaults to `false`: a page holds many entries and each map may be 64 KiB, so a listing does not carry them unless asked.

parameters.name: snapshot_id
parameters.description: Use the directory state captured by this snapshot

400.description: Invalid path, limit, cursor, include_attributes, snapshot id, or non-snapshot checkpoint

404.description: Namespace, path, or snapshot not found

410.description: Namespace deleted or snapshot released or expired

get.description: Returns path metadata from the current state or a live snapshot.

parameters.name: include_attributes
parameters.description: Project the inode's attribute map and revision (`true` or `false`). Defaults to `true`: a stat answers for one path and a map is capped at 64 KiB.

parameters.name: snapshot_id
parameters.description: Use the path state captured by this snapshot

400.description: Invalid path, include_attributes, snapshot id, or non-snapshot checkpoint

404.description: Namespace, path, or snapshot not found

410.description: Namespace deleted or snapshot released or expired

get.description: Resolves the current path to a file inode and returns revisions for that file. If the file could be renamed, use the inode revision API for stable identity.

Returns the namespace's recoverable deletions, oldest deletion first. Entries never age out at the retention floor; each carries the inode id and deletion sequence undelete needs, plus the deleted name when the delete recorded one.

post.description: Creates a new namespace as a fork from the source namespace's current durable view.

get.description: Searches file content with a regular expression, accelerated by the namespace's grep index. Matches are verified against the real pattern and returned in ascending `(inode_id, byte_offset)` order; revisions committed after the index watermark are scanned exhaustively unless `allow_stale` skips them. Requires this deployment to serve grep and the namespace to carry a materialized active grep root.

parameters.name: pattern
parameters.description: Pattern in the Rust `regex` crate's dialect. Its UTF-8 encoding must be at most 1024 bytes.

parameters.name: path_prefix
parameters.description: Complete absolute path used to restrict matches.

parameters.name: allow_scan
parameters.description: Permit a capped exhaustive scan when the pattern has no required grams (`true` or `false`). Defaults to `false`.

parameters.name: allow_stale
parameters.description: Return indexed-only results when the unindexed tail exceeds the scan budget (`true` or `false`). Defaults to `false`.

400.description: Invalid pattern, cursor, or an unindexable pattern without allow_scan

500.description: The grep index is corrupt or its backing store is unavailable

501.description: This deployment does not serve grep queries, the grep index is not enabled, or its backfill has not completed on this namespace

get.description: Returns the current path entry for a visible inode. Unknown or hidden inodes answer `inode_not_found`.

parameters.name: include_attributes
parameters.description: Project the inode's attribute map and revision (`true` or `false`). Defaults to `true`: a stat answers for one path and a map is capped at 64 KiB.

404.description: Namespace or visible inode not found

get.description: Lists one page of a directory's children addressed by parent inode ID, in canonical name-key order. Inode addressing keeps a listing and its resumption on the same directory across concurrent renames or moves of the parent.

parameters.name: include_attributes
parameters.description: Project each entry's attribute map and revision (`true` or `false`). Defaults to `false`: a page holds many entries and each map may be 64 KiB, so a listing does not carry them unless asked.

400.description: Invalid inode ID, limit, cursor, or include_attributes

404.description: Namespace or visible inode not found

get.description: Returns retained revisions for a file inode without requiring a current path.

400.description: Invalid inode ID, limit, or cursor

get.description: Reads and verifies one retained file revision by inode ID and revision number.

400.description: Invalid inode ID or revision number

404.description: Namespace, inode, or revision not found

post.description: Authorizes a direct read of one retained inode revision. The request body is `{}` and the response does not include a path.

400.description: Invalid inode ID, revision number, or request body

404.description: Namespace, inode, or revision not found

get.description: Lists live snapshots in snapshot-id order. Released and expired snapshots are omitted.

400.description: Invalid namespace id, limit, or cursor

post.description: Creates a snapshot of the current namespace state. Every call creates a new snapshot.

400.description: Invalid namespace id, name, or ttl

post.description: Extends a live snapshot without passing its lifetime limit. Repeating the request has the same result.
Releases a snapshot by id. Repeated releases succeed.
Starts an upload session for content that may later be attached to a file. Service-proxied uploads send bytes through the server; direct-put uploads return object-store presigned credentials.

413.description: Body exceeds the 1 MiB upload-control limit

get.description: Returns an upload session. A completed session includes a new content token so the client can retry the commit without uploading the content again.

post.description: Ends an upload session without selecting content and deletes the object it was writing. Repeating it succeeds; a session that already completed cannot be aborted.
Completes an upload. The request mode must match the mode used to start the session. Direct uploads include a content claim; multipart also includes completed parts.

requestBody.description: The request mode must match the upload session.

413.description: Completion body exceeds the advertised `upload.completion_max_body_bytes` limit

put.description: Uploads bytes into a service-proxied upload session and returns the content reference for the stored object.

post.description: Returns one short-lived, checksum-bound upload capability per requested part of an open direct_multipart session. Asking again for a part is how a client retries it.

413.description: Body exceeds the 1 MiB upload-control limit

AbsolutePath.description: Validated complete absolute namespace path, serialized as a plain string.

ActorId.description: Opaque hosting-platform actor id: non-empty, at most 256 UTF-8 bytes, without leading or trailing whitespace or control characters.

ActorKind.description: The type of actor responsible for a commit.

ActorRef.description:
Identifies the user, service, or system responsible for a commit.

LoonFS stores this value as provided. It does not authenticate the actor or
look up profile information.

id.description: A stable identifier supplied by the application.

AdvanceRetentionRequest.description: An option-free request that selects retention-floor advancement.

AdvanceRetentionResponse.description: Result of advancing the retention floor.

retention_floor_seq.description: New minimum sequence for incremental replay.

AttributeKey.description:
A validated inode attribute name from 1 to 128 UTF-8 bytes without control characters.

Names are byte-exact; writes reject the reserved `loonfs.` prefix even though
the type accepts it.

AttributeRevisionNo.description: Revision number for an inode's attributes. It starts at 0 and increases whenever the attribute map changes.

AttributeValue.description:
A validated inode attribute value of at most [`MAX_ATTRIBUTE_VALUE_BYTES`] UTF-8 bytes.

Empty strings and control characters are valid, and only an explicit remove
operation deletes an attribute.

Attributes.description:
A validated attribute map limited to [`MAX_ATTRIBUTE_ENTRIES`] entries and
[`MAX_ATTRIBUTES_TOTAL_BYTES`] total key and value UTF-8 bytes.

Construction and decoding reject values over these limits; an empty map
represents cleared attributes.

access.description: Short-lived provider access without the raw object key.

inode_id.description: Stable inode ID within a namespace

A presigned URL for one content object.

The URL expires at `access.expires_at_ms`; later path changes do not change the object.

content_ref.description: The identity, byte length, and checksum of the object to download.

CapabilityDocument.description: The profiles, features, and limits advertised by a deployment.

features.description: The named features supported by this deployment, with absent keys treated as unsupported.

limits.description: Advisory numeric limits clients may use to pre-validate requests.

profiles.description: The advertised `plane/version` profiles, each with every required operation implemented.

ChangeSeq.description: Sequence number assigned to a namespace commit. It determines the order in which commits become visible.

Checkpoint.description: One checkpoint resource described by its durable record.

checkpoint_id.description: Durable checkpoint id used to address the checkpoint for release.

checkpoint_seq.description: Sequence covered by the checkpoint's pinned basis.

created_at_ms.description: Time the checkpoint record was created, in Unix milliseconds.

expires_at_ms.description: The automatic release time in Unix milliseconds, or `None` until an explicit release.

owner.description: Who owns the checkpoint, including the label carried by a user pin.

CheckpointId.description:
Durable checkpoint identifier.

A checkpoint is a durable bookmark to a namespace manifest version.

CheckpointOwnerSummary.description: The owner of a checkpoint record.

Checksum.description: A checksum algorithm and its canonical lowercase hexadecimal value.

value.description: The canonical lowercase hexadecimal checksum without a prefix.

CommitId.description:
Client-supplied idempotency key for one logical commit.

Reuse the same `CommitId` when retrying the same request. The accepted
grammar is 1 to 128 lowercase ASCII letters, digits, dots, underscores,
or hyphens, starting with a letter or digit. [`CommitId::generate`] returns
`c_<32 lowercase hex>`, but callers may supply any value in that grammar.

CommitRequest.description:
A request to commit one or more filesystem operations atomically in order.

Unknown fields are rejected.

actor.description: Actor responsible for the commit, as supplied by the application.

commit_id.description: Caller-supplied idempotency key for the whole request.

content_tokens.description: The proofs for new external content references in this request.

message.description: The caller annotation that forms part of the commit identity.

operations.description: The non-empty ordered operations to commit atomically.

CommitResponse.description: The result of one commit, including its attribution and filesystem events.

commit_id.description: The idempotency key for the commit.

committed_at_ms.description: The commit time in Unix milliseconds; `committed_seq` defines commit order.

committed_by.description: Actor responsible for the commit, as supplied by the application.

committed_seq.description: Sequence number where the commit became visible.

events.description:
The filesystem events in commit order, or `None` when replaying a commit
without retained WAL history.

message.description: The optional caller annotation for the commit.

CommittedChange.description: One committed change in namespace order.

commit_id.description: Client idempotency key for this logical commit.

committed_at_ms.description: The commit time in Unix milliseconds; `committed_seq` defines commit order.

committed_by.description: Actor responsible for the commit, as supplied by the application.

committed_seq.description: Namespace sequence for this logical commit.

CompletedUploadPart.description: One uploaded part accepted by the object-store provider.

checksum.description: Checksum the part was signed and accepted with.

etag.description: Entity tag the provider returned for the accepted part.

ContentId.description:
Durable identity of one immutable content object.

The body is 128 fully random bits, with no time component: content
object keys shard on the id's leading characters, and a clock-derived
prefix would put every upload in one window into one shard. The id
names *which object*, never what it contains — integrity evidence
rides [`crate::ContentRef`] beside it.

ContentRef.description:
A reference to one immutable content object.

The object must be durable before the reference is published.

checksum.description: Mandatory checksum over the complete object.

content_id.description: Immutable identity of the referenced object.

kind.description: Content strategy used by the referenced object.

size_bytes.description: Complete byte length of the referenced content.

ContentToken.description: Proof that a specific `content_ref` may be used in a later commit.

token.description: The opaque server-signed token that clients must not parse.

ttl_ms.description: The checkpoint lifetime in milliseconds, or `None` for an explicit release only.

name.description: A label that does not need to be unique.

MaintenanceStepRequest.description:
The actions selected for one explicit maintenance step.

The request must select at least one action, and unknown fields are rejected.

gc.description: The optional bounded mark-and-sweep garbage-collection action.

metadata_maintenance.description: The optional WAL flush and bounded metadata reorganization action.

retention.description: The optional action that advances the retention floor to the flushed manifest head.

MaintenanceStepResponse.description:
The result of one explicit maintenance step.

Each field is present only when the request selected its action.

retention.description: Where the retention floor ended up.

status_before.description: Namespace diagnostics observed before the step acted.

NamespaceId.description:
Durable id for one namespace.

A namespace is one filesystem history. This id is not a display name and
should not be reused after destruction. Its serialized form is 1 to 128
lowercase ASCII letters, digits, dots, underscores, or hyphens, starting
with a letter or digit; the `loonfs-` prefix is reserved for system use.

Metadata for one path returned by stat and directory listings.

Attribute fields are included only when requested.
